init.title: Polling budget
init.description:
Set the maximum number of Tesla Fleet API calls per month. The integration auto-tunes its polling from this number: each refresh fetches **today + this month**, and less often **this year + lifetime** (the slower one runs on a fraction of cycles).

At {current}/month: today refreshes about every {today_minutes} min, year/lifetime about every {year_hours} h (≈ {est_calls} calls/month). The Fleet API free allowance is 5,000 calls/month.

**Stale-data threshold** — when a site stops reporting, Tesla keeps returning HTTP 200 with zeroed buckets, so nothing looks broken. If no production has been reported for this many hours, the *Data problem* sensor turns on. Lower catches outages sooner; raise it if genuinely zero-output days trip it.

**Live status** — also poll the site's live status each refresh. This is the only way to tell whether the site is reporting to Tesla *at all*: it timestamps when the gateway last checked in, which stays meaningful at night when production is legitimately zero. It costs one extra call per refresh, so at a fixed budget it roughly halves how often everything updates — in exchange for being able to spot an outage in the dark.

application_credentials.description: Create a Tesla developer application at the [Tesla developer dashboard]({developer_dashboard_url}) and paste its Client ID and Client Secret here. Make sure the app's allowed origin/redirect includes your Home Assistant My redirect URL, and that the `energy_device_data` scope is enabled.
